text.p: Roberts Pharmaceutical Corp said on Monday it received notification from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration that its new drug application for Agrylin, a drug to reduce excess platelets, was approvable.
Roberts developed Agrylin, or anagrelide hydrochloride, to treat essential thrombocythemia, a life threatening condition characterized by high blood platelet counts.

Agrylin capsules are indicated for the treatment of patients with essential thrombocythemia to reduce the elevated platelet count, to reduce the risk of thrombosis and to improve associated symptoms, the company said.
As a prerequisite to marketing clearance, Roberts said it would give the FDA copies of the product's final printed labeling. It said it expected to market the product near-term.
